binding.text: āśā as grasping / clinging hope — goaded toward a specific outcome or object; the downward pull of attached desire
praśraya / praṇāśa — giving latitude to the point of dissolution; unrestrained indulgence that runs to annihilating collapse
ghṛṇā — the fetter of hatred / revulsion: hatred arising (mainly from frustrated moha) and the downward pull toward the crude (pat / patati -> downfall)
artha as possessive acquisition — worldly purpose pursued and possessed as acquisition, status or control (rajasic grasping to acquire)
envy — the sting at another's success; covetous resentment at another's good fortune

liberating.text: aspiring hope held WITHOUT attachment — forward-orientation that acts while releasing the grip on the result (oriented toward the Great, not the object)
disciplined containment that holds form — latitude restrained and sublimated so the dissolving tendency is contained rather than annihilating
the upward turn — goodwill that dissolves revulsion; anurakti (attraction for the Great) consummating in devotion (ūrdhva gam)
purposeful action without possessive bondage — rajasic energy directed to legitimate purpose/means without clinging (artha pursued without attachment)
muditā — sympathetic gladness at another's fortune; rejoicing in others' good rather than being stung by it
